title: Unlike the fine deeds of unbelievers
source_text: XI. Neque solum a peccatis manifestis, id est, actionibus per se malis & lege vetitis differunt bona fidelium opera: sed etiam ab ipsis infidelium egregie factis, quae speciem virtutis habent, & civiliter bona ac laudabilia sunt. Etenim in ejusmodi actibus infidelium, quibus virtutem aliquam exercere videntur, puta benignitatis, justitiae & temperantiae, substantia quidem actionis bona est, veruntamen actio simpliciter est mala: quia non procedit ab eo principio a quo manare debent actiones omnes vere bonae & sanctae, scilicet, a Dei amore: neque tendit in finem ad quem spectare debent eaedem actiones, nimirum ad Dei gloriam. Sed fidelium opera per gratiam Dei facta ad gloriam Dei tendunt, & ex charitate procedunt. Ideoque actiones illae infidelium, utut hominum judicio speciosae videantur, Deo gratae & acceptae non sunt: nec quicquam authoribus suis ad salutem aeternam prosunt. Sed fidelium opera Deo grata atque accepta sunt, & aeternae salutis remunerationem ab eo accipiunt.
pass_a_gloss: XI. Nor do the good works of the faithful differ only from manifest sins, that is, from actions evil in themselves & forbidden by the law: but also from the very deeds of unbelievers excellently done, which have the appearance of virtue, & are civilly good & praiseworthy. For in such acts of unbelievers, in which they seem to exercise some virtue, say of kindness, justice & temperance, the substance of the action indeed is good, but yet the action is simply evil: because it does not proceed from that principle from which all truly good & holy actions ought to flow, namely, from the love of God: nor does it tend to the end at which the same actions ought to aim, namely to the glory of God. But the works of the faithful done through the grace of God tend to the glory of God, & proceed from charity. And therefore those actions of unbelievers, however fair they may seem in the judgement of men, are not pleasing & acceptable to God: nor do they profit their authors anything for eternal salvation. But the works of the faithful are pleasing & acceptable to God, & receive from him the reward of eternal salvation.
pass_b_english: Thesis XI. The good works of believers differ not only from open sins, that is, from actions that are evil in themselves and forbidden by the law. They also differ from the fine deeds of unbelievers that look like virtue and are good and praiseworthy by civic standards.

When unbelievers seem to practise some virtue, such as kindness, justice or self-control, the substance of the act is good, but the act as a whole is simply bad. It does not come from the source all truly good and holy actions must come from, the love of God, and it does not aim at the goal they must aim at, the glory of God.

Believers' works, done by God's grace, aim at God's glory and come from love. So those acts of unbelievers, however impressive they look to human judgment, are not pleasing or acceptable to God, and they do their doers no good at all for eternal salvation. Believers' works are pleasing and acceptable to God, and he rewards them with eternal salvation.

choices.why: Le Blanc's thesis: the works of the regenerate are truly, not just apparently, good, even though they are not perfect.
